findings.text: follow-on: the sweep tests replace dispatch_review_for_run with a stub (line 44) and assert on the stub's call list, so the end-to-end guarantee "no launch occurs for the project the caller did not name" is assembled from a scoping case over the classification list plus a separate lane case that calls dispatch_review_for_run directly; the project-filter mutation does falsify the scoping, but an integration case driving the real dispatch_review_for_run through recover's scope would cover both in one run.

item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit against 4c28566915dc727e67df7dbc54cb27aa1d145e17; 9db44ea6 adds the failing-scope test file, cb6a0601 adds the --dispatch-reviews option, the scoping refusal, the follower-liveness gate and the local-lane preference in recovery.py, and 6edf45eb adds the evidence fragment and sharpens the lane comment without touching behaviour.
item_verdicts.done_when: the six-file scoped gate at base 4c28566915dc727e67df7dbc54cb27aa1d145e17 is 10 failed/412 passed EXIT=1 and at head 6edf45ebb457bd75d5ee8b62aac40bf5b43e6b84 is 1 failed/421 passed EXIT=1, the single remaining failure (tests/test_crew_recovery.py::test_cli_follow_streams_each_event_as_one_json_document) failing at the base arm too; my own extraction of the head tree runs tests/test_recover_launches_only_what_it_is_asked.py 9 passed, and of the base tree with that file added 9 failed, so the nine cases are red at base and green at head and no failure id is added.
item_verdicts.goal: plan section 12 asks that crew recover launch nothing it was not asked to and that its help say what it launches; recover() now defaults to zero launches and raises CrewError unless both dispatch_reviews and a named project are supplied (reckon/crew/recovery.py:10425), skips any scoring run whose dispatching session has no live follower and records it awaiting-coordinator (reckon/crew/recovery.py:10463), and prefers the local lane absent a node declaration (reckon/crew/recovery.py:2122), while the help first line and the recover() docstring now both read "launch reviews only with --dispatch-reviews and --project" (reckon/cli.py:6387).
item_verdicts.manifest: read; status complete, baseline_suite records 10 failed/412 passed and after_suite 1 failed/421 passed each with completed true, their revisions match their log headers (gate-base.log revision=4c28566915dc727e67df7dbc54cb27aa1d145e17, gate-head-final.log revision=6edf45ebb457bd75d5ee8b62aac40bf5b43e6b84), the added-failure count derives to zero, and the negative control records one mutant failure EXIT=1.
item_verdicts.write_paths: git show --stat over 9db44ea6, cb6a0601 and 6edf45eb touches exactly reckon/crew/recovery.py, reckon/cli.py, tests/test_recover_launches_only_what_it_is_asked.py and docs/evidence/fragments/scoring-should-stop-a-promotion/recover-launches-only-what-it-is-asked.html; the docs/figures directory named in the write scope holds no file and nothing outside those four paths changed.

justifications.durability: the boundaries are each held by a case (unscoped refusal, scoped default, opted-in scope, departed session, help, lane selection) and the project-filter mutation reddens the two-project case, but the sweep-level cases stub dispatch_review_for_run (tests/test_recover_launches_only_what_it_is_asked.py:44), so the scoping guarantee is proved on the classification list rather than by driving the real dispatch through recover.
justifications.evidence: gate-base.log at 4c28566915dc727e67df7dbc54cb27aa1d145e17 shows the nine new cases among 10 failures and gate-head-final.log at 6edf45ebb457bd75d5ee8b62aac40bf5b43e6b84 shows them green with 421 passed, my independent base extraction reproduces the unscoped launch with 9 failed and the head extraction gives 9 passed, and the negative control log records the project-filter mutation failing its named-project case EXIT=1.
justifications.fit: the new dispatch_reviews flag threads through recover() and the CLI in the module's existing keyword idiom, the docstring and click help are made to agree on one first line, and the recorded ruff delta is the same 14 findings at both arms over the changed paths.
justifications.goal_fidelity: recover() returns zero launches by default and gates both a named project and --dispatch-reviews in one guard (reckon/crew/recovery.py:10425), the help first line names the launch (reckon/cli.py:6387), and the departed-session path reports awaiting-coordinator rather than dispatching under a dead name (reckon/crew/recovery.py:10463), which is the whole of section 12's remedy; one point is held back only because a scoped caller can still reach a launch path with a live session without a second confirmation.
justifications.scope_discipline: the three commits change only the four paths named in the dispatch's write scope, no figure is claimed, and the prefer_local parameter defaults to False so the continuous reflex caller at reckon/crew/recovery.py:3709 keeps its old lane behaviour untouched.
